record.paper_title: Open Problem: Tight Bounds for Kernelized Multi-Armed Bandits with Bernoulli Rewards
record.context_brief: Logarithmic regret for finite kernelized Bernoulli bandits
record.original_question: For a finite-action kernelized Bernoulli bandit under the RKHS regularity conditions f in H_k, ||f||_{H_k} <= B, and k(x,x) <= 1, can one design regret-minimization algorithms whose regret grows logarithmically in the horizon T and whose instance-dependent dependence is governed by the Bernoulli KL divergence d(f(x), f(x*)) between each action's mean and the optimal mean f(x*)? Can such a logarithmic, KL-dependent guarantee be achieved in the kernelized setting where the kernel may encode correlations among arms, noting that the trivial kernel k(x,x') = 1{x = x'} reduces the finite kernelized bandit to an unstructured multi-armed bandit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite set of actions and let $k:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a positive-definite kernel with associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) $\mathcal{H}_k$. Assume the normalization $k(x,x)\le 1$ for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$. Let $f\in\mathcal{H}_k$ be an unknown reward function with $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_k}\le B$ for a known constant $B>0$, and assume $f(x)\in[0,1]$ for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$.

Consider the following sequential decision problem (a kernelized Bernoulli bandit): at each round $t=1,\dots,T$, the learner selects an action $x_t\in\mathcal{X}$ based on past observations and observes a Bernoulli reward $r_t\in\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{E}[r_t\mid x_t]=f(x_t)$. Let $x^\star\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}}f(x)$ and define the (pseudo-)regret
$$R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f(x^\star)-f(x_t)\bigr).$$
For Bernoulli means $p,q\in(0,1)$, let $d(p,q)=p\log(p/q)+(1-p)\log((1-p)/(1-q))$ denote the Bernoulli Kullback–Leibler divergence.

For the classical unstructured multi-armed bandit (recovered by the kernel $k(x,x')=\mathbf{1}\{x=x'\}$), the KL-UCB algorithm attains
$$\mathbb{E}[R_T]\le O\!\Bigg(\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}:\,f(x)<f(x^\star)}\frac{\log T}{d(f(x),f(x^\star))}\Bigg).$$

Question. Does there exist an algorithm for the finite-action kernelized Bernoulli bandit (with general kernel $k$ satisfying the assumptions above) whose expected regret, for every $f\in\mathcal{H}_k$ with $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_k}\le B$, satisfies an instance-dependent bound of the form
$$\mathbb{E}[R_T]\le O\!\Bigg(\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\frac{\log T}{d(f(x),f(x^\star))}\Bigg)$$
(or another bound that is logarithmic in $T$ and whose instance-dependent dependence is governed by the Bernoulli KL divergences $d(f(x),f(x^\star))$, while properly exploiting the correlations among arms encoded by $k$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2024 work on tight bounds for kernelized bandits with Bernoulli rewards. No subsequent publication resolving the logarithmic, KL-dependent regret guarantee for finite-action kernelized Bernoulli bandits was identified; the obstruction (martingale/MGF-based KL concentration not extending to correlated kernelized arms) appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Tight Bounds for Bernoulli Rewards
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open question whether tight results can be obtained for KBs.
status_evidence.claim: The Bernoulli kernelized setting lacks tight KL-type results.
